description: Returns up to 25 masked sample rows (10 by default) for an audience or a count id, each with verification badges, why it matches and a provenance card. Use it after count_audience to show the user what the records look like before quoting. Free: emails and phones are masked on the server, a repeat returns the same rows, and no rows come back when the count is under 25. Call quote_order next to price the records. Lawful basis is UK GDPR Article 6(1)(f) legitimate interests; email audiences include corporate subscribers only by default (PECR), so sole traders and ordinary partnerships are left out unless the toggle is changed.

AllGroup.description: AND: every node inside must match.

AnyGroup.description: OR: at least one node inside must match.

Audience.description: Who you want, as filters grouped by entity (company., site., contact., email., phone., signal.). The server fills its defaults (active companies, named emails, corporate subscribers, the current dataset_version) and returns the effective definition with every count.

dataset.description: The dataset an audience draws from. uk_contacts is live; ie_contacts and global_contacts are listed but not yet served.

dataset_version.description: The weekly build to count against, such as 2026-W39. Left out, the current version is filled in and returned.

dedupe.description: none keeps every matching contact, one_per_company keeps one contact per company, one_per_site keeps one per site. Default none.

schema.description: The definition's namespace and version. Older versions are upgraded by a pure function.

where.description: The filters. Left out, the audience is the whole dataset after the defaults.

Audience.title: MyDataHub audience definition (mydatahub.audience/1)

anyOf.description: Format: an audience id: aud_ followed by a 26 character ULID in upper case Crockford base32, such as aud_01JB4H2K9V6XN3M9R6T1Y5W8ZA.

AudienceRef.description: An audience definition (mydatahub.audience/1) inline, or the aud_ id of a saved audience.

BetweenFilter.description: The field lies from one value to another inclusive, over the field's order.

from.description: A band code or a number from the field's order.

to.description: A band code or a number from the field's order.

BundleNode.description: A title bundle, resolved to its filters in the effective definition: sdm (senior decision makers), manager_and_above (managers and above), owner_managed (owner managed).

EmailPolicy.description: Email quality floor. Defaults: min_deliverability_score 70, allow_catch_all false.

allow_catch_all.description: Whether catch-all addresses count. Default false.

min_deliverability_score.description: Lowest deliverability score counted, 0 to 100. Default 70.

Filter.description: One criterion: a field from GET /v1/catalogue/filters, an operator and its operands. Exclusions nest under not.

GteFilter.description: The field is at or after the value in its order: for bands, the band and every larger one.

value.description: A band code or a number from the field's order.

InFilter.description: The field holds one of the listed codes.

items.description: A code, a rank or a boolean, as the field's catalogue lists it.

InListFilter.description: The record's hashed email, domain, phone, company number or title term is on a suppression list. Usually nested under not; each list reports the records it removed.

list_id.description: Format: a suppression list id: sup_ followed by a 26 character ULID in upper case Crockford base32, such as sup_01JB4H7Q2V7XN3M9R6T1Y5W8ZA.

LteFilter.description: The field is at or before the value in its order. Rank 1 is the most senior, so Director and above is contact.job_level_rank lte 6.

value.description: A band code or a number from the field's order.

MatchesFilter.description: Job title keyword match. mode contains (the default) or starts_with expands each term with the expansion sets; mode exact matches verbatim titles. Every expanded term is returned with the count.

exclude_terms.description: Expanded terms removed by hand. Kept in the definition so the count stays reproducible when the title dictionary changes.

expand.description: Expansion sets to apply, each once: plural_singular, department_synonyms, ampersand_and, abbreviations, permutations. Left out, the first four apply; an empty list applies none. Not used with mode exact.

mode.description: contains (the default) matches titles containing a term, starts_with matches titles beginning with it, exact takes verbatim titles with no expansion.

NotGroup.description: Negation: the single node inside must not match.

PlaceCentre.description: A named place. Ambiguous names come back from resolve_location as candidates, never a silent choice.

code.description: The ONS geography code of the chosen candidate when resolve_location found more than one, such as E08000035 for the Leeds district.

place.description: A place name, resolved with resolve_location, such as Leeds.

PointCentre.description: A latitude and longitude in WGS84 degrees.

postcode.description: The centroid of a postcode unit, sector, district or area, such as LS1 4AP.

RadiusCentre.description: The centre of a radius: a place, a postcode or a latitude and longitude.

SinceFilter.description: Within the last N days: a date field, or a Companies House signal of the listed types on signal.type.

values.description: For signal.type only: the signal types to look for, such as company.incorporated.

WhereNode.description: A group (all, any, not), a title bundle or a filter. Groups nest up to 32 deep, and a where tree holds up to 1,000 filters, groups and bundles.

WithinRadiusFilter.description: Sites within radius_miles of the centre. The count reports the centroid used and the postcodes matched.

radius_miles.description: Radius in miles, 1 to 100. Under 5 miles needs an account.

inputSchema.description: The audience or count to sample: exactly one of audience or count_id.

count_id.description: A count id instead of an audience.

shuffle.description: Draw a new seed. Counts against your rate budget and is logged. Default false, so a repeat returns the same rows.

name: preview_records

ComplianceObject.description: Carried by every preview row, order record, lookup and enrichment, and repeated as CSV columns and as the MyDataHub property group on CRM push.

examples.attribution: Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0

attribution.description: The OGL v3.0 attribution for Companies House company data. Officer names are personal data outside the OGL, so they carry article14_status instead.

corporate_subscriber.description: True for companies, LLPs, Scottish partnerships and public bodies, where the PECR regulation 22 consent rule does not apply.

lawful_basis.description: UK GDPR Article 6(1)(f) legitimate interests, with the LIA in lia_ref.

record_age_days.description: Days since the record was compiled.

subscriber_class.description: PECR subscriber class: ltd, plc, llp, scottish_partnership, public_body, charity_incorporated, sole_trader, ordinary_partnership, unknown.

tps_ctps_screened_at.description: The date of the screen the status is as of; null when not screened.

tps_ctps_status.description: Telephone screen: clear, tps_registered, ctps_registered, tps_or_ctps_registered, not_screened. The result of the screen on tps_ctps_screened_at, valid until tps_ctps_valid_until. In a sample, an order's records (each time they are fetched, downloaded or pushed) and an enrichment, a clear number reads not_screened, with no dates, once that screen is more than 28 days before the day the record is served; a registered number stays registered.

tps_ctps_valid_until.description: 28 days after tps_ctps_screened_at, when this screen stops being valid. Null when not screened. Screen the numbers you are supplied yourself before calling, and again every 28 days.

Disclosure.description: Whether these numbers are exact or protected: "under 10" cells, rounding to 5 and secondary suppression for anonymous and trial callers.

level.description: exact for authenticated paid callers; rounded for anonymous and trial callers, whose counts under 100 and every cell are rounded to the nearest 5.

rounded_to.description: 5 when numbers are rounded; null when they are exact.

secondary_suppression.description: True when cross-tab or breakdown cells of 10 or more were hidden as "suppressed" so totals cannot be differenced.

OtherBadge.description: Re-checking, unverified or suppressed, or premium_list: on the premium list as of the dataset version's as-of date (the date), on a version that records no per-record check date.

date.description: The date behind the badge, if any.

email_masked.description: First character of the local part plus the top level domain, such as j••••@••••.co.uk.

id.description: A session-scoped id standing in for the record. It never reveals contact_ ids.

job_level.description: The level, such as Director; null when the level is not known.

phone_masked.description: To the area code, such as 0113 ••• •••1.

Provenance.description: Source per entity, answering the ICO questions who compiled it and where from.

company.description: Where the company facts came from and the snapshot date.

contact.description: Who compiled the contact, when, and how it was last confirmed.

email.description: The latest email verification: date, provider result and location.

ProvenanceCard.description: The ICO due diligence answers for one record, as shown on the sample row.

sources.description: The source of each field shown, such as title: emailmovers_research.

VerificationBadge.description: A badge on a sample row. Every verified has a date.

VerifiedBadge.description: Verified, with the date it was verified.

date.description: The verification date. Every verified has one.

WhyItMatches.description: One predicate the record satisfies, with its value.

explanation.description: Such as Marketing Director matched marketing manager through expansion.

pointer.description: JSON pointer to the filter in the audience.

outputSchema.description: A free, masked sample of up to 25 rows. Repeating a sample returns the same rows.

count.description: The count the rows were drawn from, rounded as disclosure says.

count_id.description: Format: a count id: cnt_ followed by 20 base32 characters (A to Z and 2 to 7), such as cnt_7K2PQ4MAXN3R6TBY5WDZ.

dataset_version.description: The immutable weekly build a count is bound to, such as 2026-W39. The last 52 stay queryable.

id.description: Format: a preview id: prv_ followed by a 26 character ULID in upper case Crockford base32, such as prv_01JB4H3M7Q2V7XN3M9R6T1Y5W8.

seed.description: The seed the rows came from; the same audience gives the same seed.

watermark.description: The account id watermarked into sample CSVs; null when signed out.

withheld.description: Rows held back: all of them when the count is under 25, or rows whose title fewer than 10 people hold.

title: Preview sample records
